beats.text: This shrimp can stun a fish without even touching it.
The pistol shrimp snaps its giant claw shut so fast, it fires a jet of water.
That jet creates a bubble, and the bubble collapses with a loud bang.
For a split second, the inside reaches around 4,700 degrees Celsius.
That's nearly as hot as the surface of the Sun.
It even gives off a tiny flash of light. Scientists call it shrimpoluminescence.
Whole colonies crackle so loudly, they can mess with submarine sonar.
